Implement ONE complex data-integrity fix (F1) in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (Nxeon migration engine). Edit only that file. After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN (exit 0) and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` (green). Do NOT run the worker, deploy, or commit. This is the last data-loss fix — correctness and a safe fallback matter more than completeness. Read the relevant regions FIRST and understand the existing flow before editing. Report final line numbers + exactly how the dump/restore + fallback are wired.

## The problem (F1)
A Postgres/MySQL/MariaDB/Mongo running INSIDE a container has its data in a named Docker volume, and today the engine migrates it by a LIVE `rsync` of `/var/lib/docker/volumes/<v>/_data` while the source container keeps writing → a torn, possibly-corrupt datadir that the target DB may fail to recover or silently loses recent writes. The engine only does consistent logical dumps for HOST-NATIVE mysql/postgres. There is no `docker exec` dump anywhere.

## The fix: init-fresh + logical restore for containerized DBs
For a RUNNING source container whose image base is a known DB engine, replace the hot datadir copy with a consistent logical dump on the source and a restore on the target after the stack is up. Read the existing code first:
- Named-volume copy loop (search `dockerVolumes`/`volumesToCopy`, `/var/lib/docker/volumes`, `rsyncPull(...\_data...)`).
- Container inventory + env capture (search `SrcContainer`, `c.image`, `c.mounts`, `containerEnvScript`, how standalone container env is read from the source).
- Host-native DB dump/restore for reference on streaming + import patterns (search `mysqldump`, `pg_dumpall`, `pg_dump`, the `mysql <`/`psql` import, how dumps stream source→target via `onSource(...) > ${work}/dumps/...`).
- The compose empty-volume refusal just added (F3) and the F2 project-name `-p` — F1 MUST coordinate with these (below).
- Bring-up (compose ~`up -d`, standalone recreate) and the point AFTER which target containers are running.

### Detection
Identify running source containers whose image (basename, ignoring tag/registry) matches `postgres|mysql|mariadb|mongo` (reuse the same stateful regex the standalone empty-volume guard uses). For each, find its DATA named volume from `c.mounts` (the volume mounted at the engine's datadir — `/var/lib/postgresql/data`, `/var/lib/mysql`, `/data/db`).

### Credentials (read-only, from the container's own env)
Read the DB superuser creds from the container's environment on the SOURCE (the engine already reads container env — reuse that path; or `onSource(docker exec <c> printenv)` / from inspect env): Postgres `POSTGRES_USER`/`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (default user `postgres`), MySQL/Maria `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD` (or `MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD`), Mongo `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME`/`MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD`. Never put a password in argv or a log — pass via env/`--env-file`/stdin, consistent with how the engine already handles container env (0600 files, values never printed). This is READ-ONLY on the source (a dump reads); it does not violate the source read-only guard, but verify your `docker exec … pg_dump/mysqldump/mongodump` commands are pure reads and will pass `assertSourceReadOnly` (they run via `onSource`).

### Dump (source → target work dir), during the copy phase
- Postgres: `docker exec <c> pg_dumpall -U <user>` (carries roles+all DBs) streamed to `${work}/dumps/<c>.pgdump` (mirror the host-native pg streaming).
- MySQL/Maria: `docker exec <c> mysqldump --all-databases --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events` → `${work}/dumps/<c>.sql`.
- Mongo: `docker exec <c> mongodump --archive` (with auth flags) → `${work}/dumps/<c>.mongoarchive`.
Cap sizes / respect the existing transfer timeout.

### Skip the hot copy ONLY on dump success; coordinate with F3
- If the logical dump SUCCEEDS: mark that container's data volume to be SKIPPED by the hot-copy loop (the target DB will init a fresh empty datadir from its env, then we restore into it). Also mark it so the F3 compose empty-volume refusal does NOT refuse this volume (an empty datadir is EXPECTED here because a restore is pending) — thread a "willRestore" set that F3 consults.
- If the dump FAILS or creds are unreadable or the engine is unknown: DO NOT skip — keep the current hot volume copy as the fallback, and push an honest WARNING step that the DB volume was copied live and may be inconsistent (recommend a manual dump). Never end up with a skipped copy AND no restore (that would be an empty DB).

### Restore (target), AFTER the DB container/stack is up
After bring-up, for each successfully-dumped DB: wait for the target DB container to be running/healthy (poll with a bounded backoff), then restore via `docker exec -i <targetContainer>`:
- Postgres: `psql -U <user>` < the dump (pg_dumpall output includes CREATE DATABASE/roles).
- MySQL: `mysql` < the dump.
- Mongo: `mongorestore --archive` < the archive.
Identify the TARGET container (the recreated same-named container / the compose service). Report each restore as its own step (running/failed with how to check). If the restore fails, name it clearly — do NOT report the migration clean.

## Constraints
- SAFETY FIRST: the fallback path (hot copy + warn) must be bulletproof — any uncertainty → fall back, never skip-without-restore.
- Reuse existing helpers (streaming, `onSource`, env-file handling, container name resolution, the stateful regex, `report`/`push`). Validate every interpolated value; single-quoted `sh -c '…'`; secrets never in argv/logs.
- Do not regress F2/F3/A1 or the compose/web work already in the file.
- Finish only when tsc is clean and the consolidate test passes. Report: detection, cred source, the three dump commands, how you SKIP the volume copy + coordinate with F3's "willRestore", where the restore runs, and the exact fallback behavior.

## Summary

Implemented the init-fresh + logical-restore fix for containerised databases in `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts` only. `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 and `test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` passes 18/18. All generated shell fragments were verified to parse under both `sh -n` and `dash -n`.

### What was added / where (final line numbers)

**Module-level helpers (lines 2080–2178):**
- `dbEngineInfo(image)` (2080) — classifies an image basename (registry/tag/digest stripped) as `postgres|mariadb|mysql|mongo` and returns its datadir (`/var/lib/postgresql/data`, `/var/lib/mysql`, `/data/db`), dump extension and label. `null` for anything else (redis, postgis, …), so those safely keep the hot copy — consistent with the existing stateful regex.
- `containerDbDumpScript(priv, container, engine)` (2102) — the source-side dump, emitted as a plain-string script.
- `containerDbReadyCommand(container, engine)` (2132) — target-side readiness probe.
- `containerDbRestoreCommand(container, engine, dumpPath, errPath)` (2153) — target-side restore.

**Dump during the copy phase (lines 5527–5580):** For every RUNNING `srcContainer` whose image is a known DB engine and whose datadir is a named volume (matched from `c.mounts` kind `volume` by dest == datadir, allowing ancestor/child dest), it streams a consistent dump via `putScript`+`onSourceScript` into `${work}/dumps/db-<c>.<ext>` (mirrors the host-native `onSource(...) > dump` streaming). The `volumesToCopy` list gained `.filter((v) => !restoreVolumes.has(v))` (5579) to skip the hot copy only on dump success.

**Restore after bring-up (lines 6737–6800), placed after the standalone-container loop and before the 9d space-reclaim** — so both compose `up -d` and standalone recreation have already run.

### The three dump commands (all via `docker exec`, run through `onSource`/`assertSourceReadOnly` as pure reads)
- Postgres: `docker exec <c> sh -c 'PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" pg_dumpall -U "${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}"'` (carries roles + all DBs).
- MySQL/Maria: `docker exec <c> sh -c 'MYSQL_PWD="${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD:-${MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}}" mysqldump -u root --all-databases --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events'`.
- Mongo: `docker exec <c> sh -c 'mongodump --archive'` with `--username/--password/--authenticationDatabase admin` added when `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME` is set.

### Credential source (never in argv / never logged)
Read READ-ONLY from the container's own environment by NAME inside the container's shell (`$POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `MYSQL_PWD` env, `$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD`). `docker exec` already exposes the container's configured env, so the password value never enters this process, never appears on any command line on either host, and never reaches a log. The single quotes in each `sh -c '…'` are safe because the dump goes over `onSourceScript` (streamed on stdin, not argv-wrapped); the ready/restore commands run on the target where single quotes are the established pattern.

### Skip + F3 coordination (the `willRestore` thread)
A `restoreVolumes: Set<string>` (line 5541) is populated only on dump SUCCESS. It:
1. Removes the datadir volume from `volumesToCopy` (5579), so the target engine inits a fresh empty datadir.
2. Is consulted by BOTH F3 empty-volume refusals — the compose path (guard added at 6496: `if (restoreVolumes.has(name)) continue;`) and the standalone path (6679) — so an empty datadir is treated as EXPECTED (restore pending) instead of being hard-refused.

### Restore (lines 6746–6800)
For each successful dump: the target container is resolved by `docker ps --filter volume=<vol>` (robust across compose project-prefixing and standalone recreation), falling back to the same-named container. It then polls the engine with bounded backoff `[3,5,8,13,21,30]s`, and streams the dump into `docker exec -i <tc>` (`psql` / `mysql --force` / `mongorestore --archive --drop`). Each restore is its own step: `running` on success, `failed` (with the error tail and the exact manual command) on failure — the migration is never reported clean on a failed restore.

### Fallback behavior (bulletproof, never skip-without-restore)
- Dump fails / creds unreadable / not a known engine / datadir isn't a named volume → the volume is NOT added to `restoreVolumes`, so the existing hot `rsync` copy stands as the fallback, plus an honest `copied`-status WARNING that the live copy may be inconsistent and to take a manual dump.
- Dump succeeds but the target container never comes up (e.g. F3 project-name mismatch causing a loud refusal) → the restore loop reports a `failed` step ("database is EMPTY, dump kept at …") — loud, never silent. There is no path that skips the copy and also silently skips the restore.
